scope: Explicit cancellation at streamed PDF patch boundaries
implementation: A lazy patch iterator checks cancellation before advancing and before allocating a new triangle chunk. Cancellation yields one explicit error and terminates the stream. The sampler refuses that error rather than treating cancellation as normal end-of-input. This preserves failure even when a synthetic predicate returns true only once.
verified: Every observed checkpoint across a three-patch stream cancels without accepting a partial map.
Early cancellation performs no patch generation; a cancelled iterator emits one error and then terminates.
Nine-component scratch reservations are released at every cancellation checkpoint and after successful sampling.
limitations: One fixed-size patch subdivision is still indivisible internally.
No measured wall-clock cancellation bound or complete viewer navigation race qualification.
The full 100-format, HDR and NVIDIA/CUDA objective remains incomplete.
